Rashi on Megillah 12a:10:1.english: Is there favoritism here - How did they merit a miracle:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:10:2.english: They did [it] for appearance - Out of fear:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:12:1.hebrew: חרי חרי - מעשה מחט, מלאכת המצעות היתה עשויה נקבים נקבים:
Rashi on Megillah 12a:12:1.english: Many holes [ḥarei ḥarei] - Needlework; the work of the spreads was made [with] many holes:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:12:2.english: White wool - Chur [is] an expression of chivar [meaning white]:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:13:1.hebrew: הראוי לכסף כו' - "מטות זהב וכסף" קדריש: שר הראוי לזהב — לזהב, וגרוע — לכסף:
Rashi on Megillah 12a:13:1.english: One who is fit for silver, etc. - [Rabbi Yehudah] is expounding [the verse], "couches of gold and silver": a minister who was fit for gold [sat on] gold, and an inferior one [on] silver:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:14:1.hebrew: מתחוטטות על בעליהן - רצפה עשה להם באבנים חטוטות, כלומר שלא באו לידי אדם אלא בטורח, שמחטטים ומחזירים בעליהן אחריהן עד שמוצאין אותן בדמים יקרים:
Rashi on Megillah 12a:14:1.english: [That] are searched after by their owners - He [Ahasuerus] made a pavement for them of sought-after stones — that is to say, [stones] that do not come into a person's hands except with toil, as their owners search and go around after them until they find them at a high price:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:14:2.hebrew: וכן הוא אומר - שהמקרא משבח אבני' יקרות, ואומר: על נסיונות הרבה הן באין, "כי אבני נזר מתנוססות על אדמתו". והכתוב מדבר לישראל לעתיד לבוא, שיהיו חשובין ויקרים בין האומות כאבני נזר המתנוססות:
Rashi on Megillah 12a:14:2.english: And similarly, it states - For Scripture praises precious stones, and says [that] they come through many trials, [as it states,] "for [they are like] the stones of a crown, glittering over His land." And the verse is speaking of Israel in the time to come, that they will be esteemed and precious among the nations like glittering stones of a crown:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:15:1.hebrew: דרי דרי - שורות שורות סביב, וסוחרת לשון סחור סחור:
Rashi on Megillah 12a:15:1.english: Darei darei - Rows [and] rows around, and "soḥaret" [is] an expression [meaning] "seḥor seḥor" [around and around]:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:15:2.english: As at midday - And this [word], "and socharet" [in the verse], is an expression of sahara [the moon/light].

Rashi on Megillah 12a:15:3.english: That he proclaimed a remission for all the merchants - he brought relief to the people of his kingdom, to remove from them the tax on merchants.

Rashi on Megillah 12a:16:1.english: The early ones - meaning, Belshazzar and his company.

Rashi on Megillah 12a:17:1.hebrew: כדת של תורה - אכילת מזבח מרובה משתיה: פר ושלשה עשרונים סולת לאכילה, ונסך חצי ההין:
Rashi on Megillah 12a:17:1.english: According to the law of the Torah - The consumption of the altar is greater than the drinking: a bull and three-tenths [of an ephah] of fine flour for eating, and a libation of half a hin [of wine]:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:18:1.hebrew: מיין מדינתו - יין הרגיל בו, ולא ישכרהו [ולא ישתהו] אלא לפי רצונו:
Rashi on Megillah 12a:18:1.english: From wine of his country - Wine that he is accustomed to, and it will not intoxicate him [and he will not drink it] except according to his will:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:18:2.english: According to the wish of Mordecai and Haman - They were the chief cupbearers at the feast.

Rashi on Megillah 12a:1:1.english: This is also taught [in a baraita] - that in the years of Nebuchadnezzar and Evil-merodach, a year was swallowed up [in the overlap]:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:1:2.hebrew: עוד שנה אחת לבבל - הכי איתא בסדר עולם: "ביה בליליא קטיל בלשצר מלכא ודריוש מדאה קביל מלכותא", הרי שבעים שנה מיום שמלך נבוכדנצר, שבעים חסר אחת מיום שכיבש יהויקים, ועוד שנה אחת לבבל למלאות שבעים שנה מששלט על ישראל, ועמד דריוש והשלימה; ואחריו בשנה אחרת מלך כורש בבבל, ונפקדו פקידה במקצת, שאמר "מי בכם מכל עמו יהי אלהיו עמו ויעל" וגו'. למדנו מברייתא זו: כשמת בלשצר, לא היו לכיבוש יהויקים אלא שבעים חסר אחת, ואנחנו מנינו למעלה שבעים שנה — מ"ה דנבוכדנצר, וכ"ג דאויל מרודך, ושלשה דבלשצר — הרי שנים מקוטעות היו:
Rashi on Megillah 12a:1:2.english: Still one year for Babylonia - Thus it is taught in Seder Olam: "In that night Belshazzar the king was slain, and Darius the Mede received the kingdom" — behold, seventy years from the day Nebuchadnezzar began to reign, seventy minus one from the day he conquered Jehoiakim, and [there was] still one year [left] for Babylonia to complete seventy years from when he gained dominion over Israel, and Darius arose and completed it; and after him, in another year, Cyrus reigned in Babylonia, and they [Israel] were remembered with a partial remembrance, as he said, "Whoever there is among you of all His people, may his God be with him, and let him go up," etc. We learn from this baraita [that] when Belshazzar died, there had only been seventy minus one [years] since the conquest of Jehoiakim, whereas above we counted seventy years — forty-five of Nebuchadnezzar, twenty-three of Evil-merodach, and three of Belshazzar — thus, they were partial years:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:2:1.english: I meditated in the books - [This is] an expression of counting and calculation:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:3:1.hebrew: כתיב לפי מלאות לבבל - "שבעים שנה אפקוד אתכם" — בספר ירמיה:
Rashi on Megillah 12a:3:1.english: It is written: "After the completion for Babylonia - [of] seventy years, I will remember you" — [this is] in the Book of Jeremiah:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:3:2.hebrew: וכתיב - בספר דניאל: "למלאות לחרבות ירושלם שבעים שנה, מספר השנים אשר היה דבר ה' אל ירמיה הנביא":
Rashi on Megillah 12a:3:2.english: And it is written - in the Book of Daniel [9:2]: "to accomplish for the desolations of Jerusalem seventy years, the number of years concerning which the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet."

Rashi on Megillah 12a:4:1.hebrew: לפקידה בעלמא - ואמר: "לפי מלאות לבבל שבעים שנה אפקוד אתכם", וכך היתה — שנפקדו בשנה אחת לכורש מלך פרס, שהיא שנת ע"א לכיבוש יהויקים, שפשטה בבל על ישראל:
Rashi on Megillah 12a:4:1.english: Only for being remembered - and [the verse] states: "When seventy years are completed for Babylonia, I will remember you," and so it was — for they were remembered in the first year of Cyrus, king of Persia, which was the seventy-first year from the conquest of Yehoyakim, when Babylonia invaded Israel:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:5:1.english: Mashiach [anointed] - [This means] anointed [nimshach], like anointing oil [shemen hamishchah].

Rashi on Megillah 12a:5:2.hebrew: קובל אני לך כו' - והכי קאמר: "כה אמר ה' למשיחו לכורש אשר החזקתי בימינו" וגו', "הוא יבנה את ביתי" — תרי קראי כתיבי דסמיכי אהדדי. וניקוד טעם מקרא זה מוכיח על דרש זה: שאין לך טעם זרקא במקרא שאין סגול בא אחריו, וכאן ננקד "למשיחו" בזרקא, ו"לכורש" ננקד במאריך, להפרישו ולנתקו מעם "למשיחו":
Rashi on Megillah 12a:5:2.english: I am complaining to you, etc. - And this is what [the Gemara] means: "Thus says the Lord to His anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held," etc., [and] "He shall build My House" — [these are] two verses written close to one another. And the cantillation mark of this verse proves this homiletical interpretation: for there is no zarka cantillation mark in Scripture without a segol coming after it, yet here, "to His anointed" [limshicho] is marked with a zarka, and "to Cyrus" [leChoresh] is marked with a ma'arich [a lengthening cantillation note], to separate it and disconnect it from "to His anointed" [limshicho]:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:5:3.english: Whoever is among you of all His people, etc. - And he himself did not exert himself in the matter:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:6:1.hebrew: כתיב פרס ומדי הפרתמים - סמך "הפרתמים" אצל "מדי", וכתיב "למלכי מדי ופרס", סמך "מלכי" אצל "מדי":
Rashi on Megillah 12a:6:1.english: It is written: "Persia and Media, the nobles" - [Scripture] juxtaposed "the nobles" next to "Media," and [where] it is written: "of the kings of Media and Persia," [Scripture] juxtaposed "kings of" next to "Media."

Rashi on Megillah 12a:7:1.english: Priestly vestments - [for] the vestments of the High Priest were in his possession there, which he had brought from Jerusalem:

Rashi on Megillah 12a:8:1.english: He was clever - [in] that he had the feast for those who were distant precede the feast for the residents of his city.

Rashi on Megillah 12a:9:1.english: That they prostrated before the idol - in the days of Nebuchadnezzar.

Tosafot on Megillah 12a:13:1.hebrew: אתה מטיל קנאה - וא"ת למ"ד לעיל "הראוי לגינה לגינה, הראוי לחצר לחצר", א"כ אתה מטיל קנאה בסעודה? י"ל דסבירא ליה דכיון שלא היו רואין זה את זה, ליכא קנאה:
Tosafot on Megillah 12a:13:1.english: You cast jealousy - And if you say: According to the one who said above, "One who is fit for the garden [was placed] in the garden, [and] one who is fit for the courtyard [was placed] in the courtyard," if so, you cast jealousy into the feast? One can say that he holds that since they did not see one another, there is no jealousy:

Tosafot on Megillah 12a:17:1.hebrew: כדת של תורה אכילה מרובה משתיה - והא דאמרינן בנדה (דף כד: ושם): כל שאכילתו מרובה משתייתו עצמותיו סכויין, היינו באוכל יותר מדאי:
Tosafot on Megillah 12a:17:1.english: According to the law of the Torah, the food is greater than the drink - And as for that which we say in Niddah (24b and elsewhere), "Anyone whose eating is greater than his drinking, his bones are glossy" — that [refers to] one who eats excessively:
